claims.text: Controlled nanoscale SRO precipitates introduced into YSZ will decrease its lattice thermal conductivity.
High-purity YSZ can be electronically insulating.
Thermo-mechanical processing, annealing, and doping can introduce and tune nanoscale SRO precipitates in a YSZ matrix.
Phonon transport dominates thermal conduction in YSZ under the proposed moderate-to-high-temperature conditions.
Electronic conduction in YSZ is negligible under the proposed conditions.
The processing intervention produces nanoscale SRO precipitates embedded in the YSZ matrix.
SRO precipitates act as phonon-scattering centers.
Scattering by SRO precipitates reduces phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon scattering times lower the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity.
Processed YSZ containing controlled SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than untreated YSZ.
The decrease in lattice thermal conductivity will correlate with SRO precipitate density.
The decrease in lattice thermal conductivity will correlate with SRO precipitate size.
The relationship between precipitate density and lattice thermal conductivity may become nonlinear or saturate at high precipitate densities.
The magnitude of the conductivity change depends on the uniformity and control of precipitate introduction.
Variability in precipitate formation kinetics and distribution may change the size of the thermal-conductivity effect.
